question:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1\\3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 0\\3 & 4 & 0\\1 & 5 & k\end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Evaluate $|A|$.

(b) Expand $|B|$ along the third column and express it in terms of $k$ and $|A|$.

(c) Determine $k$ if $|B|=55$, and verify the result by direct expansion along the first row.
explanation:
(a)
$$|A|=\begin{vmatrix}2 & -1\\3 & 4\end{vmatrix}=2(4)-(-1)(3)=8+3=11$$

(b)
The first two entries of the third column of $B$ are zero. Therefore, expansion along the third column gives
$$|B|=k\begin{vmatrix}2 & -1\\3 & 4\end{vmatrix}$$
Hence,
$$|B|=k|A|=11k$$

(c)
Given that $|B|=55$,
$$11k=55$$
Therefore,
$$k=5$$
For verification, substitute $k=5$ and expand along the first row:
$$|B|=2\begin{vmatrix}4 & 0\\5 & 5\end{vmatrix}-(-1)\begin{vmatrix}3 & 0\\1 & 5\end{vmatrix}+0$$
$$|B|=2(20)+(15)=55$$
Thus, $k=5$ is verified.
